subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The following topical antibiotic agent is used in treatment of burn wounds:
questions.explanation: Silver sulfadiazine is the standard topical antimicrobial for burns.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist reviews the medical chart of a patient admitted to the hospital two days age. The chart specifies the epidermal and dermal layers were completely destroyed and some of the subcutaneous tissue was damaged. This description best describes a ___ burn?
questions.explanation: Destruction of epidermis and dermis with subcutaneous damage is a full-thickness burn.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist provides preoperative training for a patient scheduled for thoracic surgery. Which activity would be most appropriate to deep vein thrombosis postsurgery?
questions.explanation: Ankle pumps promote venous return and help prevent deep vein thrombosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient rehabilitating from cardiac surgery is monitored using an arterial line. The primary purpose of an arterial line is to:

options.B: Measure heart rate and oxygen saturation of the blood

questions.explanation: An arterial line gives continuous blood pressure monitoring.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist alerts a nurse to skin breakdown on a patient's right heel. Which position would leave the patient most susceptible to additional tissue damage?
questions.explanation: In supine the heels bear weight and are most vulnerable to pressure injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient status postradical mastectomy secondary to breast cancer is referred to physical therapy. Typical intervention includes all of the following except:

options.B: Passive and active-assistive range of motion
options.C: Elevation and positioning of the upper extremity

questions.explanation: Physiotherapy after mastectomy covers measurements, range of motion and positioning; prescribing analgesics is not a physiotherapy role.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a full-thickness burn over the entire anterior aspect of the neck is examined in physical therapy. The physical therapist must plan a treatment program based on the anticipation of a possible _______ contracture: 8
questions.explanation: A burn over the anterior neck tends to produce a flexion contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Proper position of the affected area is essential for patients with burns. Proper positioning should be maintained:

options.A: Not less than twelve hours per day
options.B: Until skin grafts have been performed
options.C: Only when the patient is sleeping

questions.explanation: Anti-deformity positioning must be maintained consistently through the day.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist prepares to treat a patient in isolation by donning a mask. Which of the following solution categories would require only the use of a mask?
questions.explanation: Respiratory (droplet) isolation requires only a mask.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with one week status post left total hip replacement is diagnosed with an acute deep vein thrombosis in the left calf. The physical therapist's role in the care of a deep vein thrombosis is:

options.A: Continued gait training with an assistive device and partial weight bearing
options.B: Progressive resistive exercise for bilateral lower extremities
options.C: Patient is on bedrest with no active therapy to the left leg

questions.explanation: In acute DVT the patient rests with no active exercise of the affected leg until anticoagulated.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: To calculate % TBSA (according to the rules of nines) left lower extremity is given weightage of:
questions.explanation: Each adult lower limb accounts for 18% of body surface area.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with a full-thickness burn receives a skin graft. Immediately after the procedure the graft site requires:

options.B: Long term immobilization of one month

questions.explanation: The graft site is temporarily immobilised to allow graft take.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: While treating a patient in ward for chest care through coughing it should be ensured that:

options.B: The patient is in supine lying position
options.C: The diaphragmatic breathing is not used

questions.explanation: During coughing the therapist must avoid inducing bronchospasm.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In tracheal stimulation to elicit the cough reflex the therapist places his finger/thumb on:
questions.explanation: Tracheal stimulation is applied just above the suprasternal notch.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The mitral valve of the heart controls the:

options.A: The amount of the blood from left. Atrium to the left. Ventricle
options.B: The amount of the blood from left. Atrium to the right. Ventricle
options.C: The amount of the blood from left. Ventricle to the right. Ventricle
options.D: The amount of the blood to pulmonary artery

questions.explanation: The mitral valve controls flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A obstructive lung disease characterized by permanent dilation of the medium sized bronchi usually the fourth to ninth generations and repeat infections in these areas is known as:
questions.explanation: Permanent dilatation of medium-sized bronchi with recurrent infection is bronchiectasis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist designs an exercise program for a patient rehabilitating from cardiac surgery. During the treatment session the therapist monitors the patient's oxygen saturation rate. Which of the following would be most representative of a normal oxygen saturation rate?
questions.explanation: Normal oxygen saturation is about 95 to 100%.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist reviews the results of a pulmonary function test of a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Which of the following results is typical of a patient with COPD?

options.D: Increased forced expiratory volume in one second

questions.explanation: Residual volume is increased in COPD because of air trapping.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Therapeutic Exercise/Kisner/5th Ed./ Pg. 875

questions.question: An order is received to perform chest physical therapy on a patient status postabdominal surgery. A chart review identifies right atelectasis. The most appropriate exercise to teach the patient is:
questions.explanation: Segmental (localised) breathing exercises re-expand an atelectatic area.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient with pulmonary disease in energy conservation techniques. Which of the following techniques would be the most effective when assisting a patient to complete a selected activity without dyspnea?
questions.explanation: Pacing activities is the most effective way to complete tasks without dyspnoea.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to assist a patient to clear secretions after performing postural drainage techniques. What position would allow the patient to produce the most forceful cough?
questions.explanation: Upright sitting allows the most forceful cough.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines the viscosity and color of a sputum sample after competing postural drainage activities. The sputum is a yellowish-greenish color and is very thick. The therapist can best describe the sputum as:
questions.explanation: Thick yellow-green sputum is described as purulent.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease performs an exercise test that will stress the patient to the point of limitation. During the test the therapist monitors the patient's physiologic response to exercise. Which of the following findings would not require cessation of the testing session?

options.A: A 20 mm Hg decrease in diastolic blood pressure with an increase in workload
options.B: Systolic hypertension greater than 160 mm Hg
options.C: A PO2 of less than 55 mm Hg

questions.explanation: Systolic BP above 160 mm Hg alone does not mandate stopping; falls in BP, low PO2 and maximal dyspnoea do.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient involved in a cardiac rehabilitation program exercises on a treadmill. While exercising the patient reports his level of perceived exertion as a 7 on Borg's ten-point scale. Which words best describe the patient's rate of perceived exertion?
questions.explanation: A rating of 7 on the CR-10 Borg scale means very strong exertion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient's breath sounds though auscultation. The therapist classifies the breath sounds in a selected lung segment as absent. Which condition is not typically associated with absent breath sound?
questions.explanation: Consolidation produces bronchial breathing, not absent breath sounds.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A cardiac rehabilitation phase I program should begin 1-4 days after the patient's infarct and should consist of all of the following prior to discharge except:

options.A: Progressive resistive exercise program for the upper and lower extremities
options.B: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure during exercise

questions.explanation: Phase I includes monitored low-level activity and education but not progressive resistive exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist from a home care agency examines a 50-year-old patient diagnosed with chronic bronchitis. The patient is overweight and presents with cyanosis at the fingertips and shallow breathing. The most immediate goal would be to:

options.A: Implement a low level exercise program
options.B: Implement breathing exercises and postural drainage technique
options.D: Complete a manual muscle test of the upper and lower extremities

questions.explanation: Breathing exercises and postural drainage address cyanosis and shallow breathing first.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with an IV in the antecubital region is treated in physical therapy. The therapist would like to instruct the patient in upper extremity active range of motion exercises, but is concerned about placing excessive pressure on the infusion site. Which of the following exercises would not be indicated?
questions.explanation: Elbow flexion and extension would place pressure on an antecubital IV site.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: An 18-year-old female diagnosed with left-sided congestive heart failure is referred to physical therapy. Which objective finding is most commonly associated with left-sided heart failure?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary oedema is the typical finding of left-sided heart failure.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient in a phase I cardiac rehabilitation program begins walking with assistance. Which following monitoring techniques would not be necessary in a phase I program?
questions.explanation: EMG is not part of phase I monitoring; BP, HR and ECG are.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Secretion removal techniques are an integral component of a pulmonary rehabilitation program. What is the simplest method to clear secretions from the upper airway?
questions.explanation: Coughing is the simplest method of clearing upper-airway secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient to expire maximally after taking a maximal inspiration. The therapist can use these instructions to measure the patient's:

options.A: Expiratory reserve volume inspiratory reserve volume

questions.explanation: Maximal expiration after maximal inspiration measures vital capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient in diaphragmatic breathing exercises. Which of the following instructions would not be helpful in teaching diaphragmatic breathing?

options.A: Place your dominant handover your midrectus area
options.B: Place your nondominant handover your midsternal area
options.D: As you expire watch your lower hand rise

questions.explanation: The abdominal (lower) hand should rise on inspiration and fall on expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist volunteers to assist participants at the finish line in a 10K rod race. The race takes place on a hot and humid day and some of the race organizers are concerned about the potential for heat related disorders such as heat exhaustion and heat stroke. The most significant variables to different between heat exhaustion and heat stroke are:
questions.explanation: Mental status and skin temperature distinguish heat exhaustion from heat stroke.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist monitors patient vital signs while exercising in a phase I cardiac rehabilitation program. The patient is status postmyocardial infarction and has progressed without difficulty while involved in the program. Which of the following vital sign recordings would exceed the typical limits of a phase I program?

options.A: Heart rate elevated 18 beats/minute above resting level
options.C: Systolic blood pressure decreases by 20 mm Hg from resting level
options.D: Diastolic blood pressure less than 100 mm Hg

questions.explanation: A fall in systolic pressure of 20 mm Hg with activity exceeds phase I limits.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient status postspinal fusion is referred for chest physical therapy. The therapist instructs patient in diaphragmatic breathing exercises. Instructions are given to the patient to place his dominant handover the mid rectus abdominis area and his nondominant handover the midstream area. As the patient inhales slowly through the nose the therapist encourage the patient to:

options.A: Direct air so that the nondominant hand rises during inspiration
options.B: Direct air so that the dominant hand rise during inspiration
options.C: Direct air so that both hands rise equally during inspiration
options.D: Direct air so that both hands do not move during inspiration

questions.explanation: The abdominal (dominant) hand should rise during inspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which illness is characterized by bronchial hyper irritability that is triggered by a number of stimuli resulting in narrowing of the air passages?
questions.explanation: Bronchial hyper-irritability with reversible narrowing defines asthma.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The ratio of chest compressions to breaths during two man cardiopulmonary resuscitation is:
questions.explanation: Two-rescuer CPR in older guidelines used 15 compressions to 2 breaths.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The most appropriate standard position for bronchial drainage to the posterior basal segment of the lower lobes is:

options.A: Patient lying prone with lower extremities declined six inches
options.B: Patient in sidelying with a six inch elevation at the foot of the bed
options.C: Patient in sidelying with a twenty inch elevation at the foot of the bed
options.D: Patient lying in prone with a twenty inch elevation at the foot of the bed

questions.explanation: Posterior basal segments drain in prone with the foot of the bed raised about 20 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with cardiac disease rates the intensity of exercise as 12 using Borg's Original Rate of Perceived Exertion Scale. A rating of 12 on the perceived exertion scale would correspond to approximately ___ percent of the patient's age- adjusted maximum heart rate?
questions.explanation: A rating of 12 on the 6-20 scale corresponds to about 60% of maximum heart rate.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist position a patient in preparation for postural drainage activities. Which of the following lung segments would not require the foot of the bed to be elevated?

options.A: Anterior segments of the upper lobes
options.C: Anterior basal segments of the lower lobes
options.D: Lateral basal segments of the lower lobes

questions.explanation: Anterior segments of the upper lobes drain in supine without elevating the foot of the bed.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Therapeutic Exercise/Kisner/5th Ed./ Pg. 872-833

questions.question: A phase IV cardiac rehabilitation program can best be described as:

options.A: A program of maintenance designed to allow the patient to continue a lifelong routine of exercise and education
options.B: A program that is monitored by electrocardiogram to determine the patient's maximal heart rate and exercise tolerance
options.C: A program that allows for independent progression of exercise at home
options.D: A two to four month program based solely on exercise which allows the patient to attain the appropriate maximal heart rate for his/her age group

questions.explanation: Phase IV is the long-term maintenance phase.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is examined following a pneumectomy secondary to lung cancer. All of the following may be seen postoperatively except:

options.C: Decreased endurance with activities of daily living

questions.explanation: After pneumonectomy chest expansion is decreased, not increased.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a six-month-old infant with spina bifida. The infant suddenly begins to act strangely at the conclusion of treatment. A primary survey reveals the infant is not breathing, but does have a pulse. The most immediate response would be to:

options.D: Begin mouth to mouth and nose breathing

questions.explanation: For an infant who is not breathing but has a pulse, give mouth-to-mouth-and-nose breaths.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Therapists often elevate the foot of a treatment table to maximize the electiveness of specific postural drainage techniques. Standard postural drainage positioning of the __________ would not require elevation of the treatment table?

options.A: Anterior segments of the upper lobes
options.B: Lateral basal segments of the lower lobes
options.C: Posterior basal segments of the lower lobes

questions.explanation: The anterior segments of the upper lobes drain in supine without table elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist develops a treatment program for a patient diagnosed with cystic fibrosis. Which of the following treatment activities would be the most essential to improve ventilation?
questions.explanation: Postural drainage is the most essential treatment to improve ventilation in cystic fibrosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist monitors a patient's blood pressure during exercise. Which of the following responses would be considered normal?

options.A: Diastole pressure increases 5 mm Hg during exercise
options.B: Systolic pressure does not decline as the intensity of exercise declines
options.C: Systolic pressure does not increase during active exercise
options.D: Systolic pressure declines during exercise before the intensity of the exercise declines

questions.explanation: A small rise or no change in diastolic pressure is a normal response to exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: In order to maximize the effectiveness of postural drainage techniques for the right middle lobe a therapist should elevate the foot of the bed ______ inches?
questions.explanation: The right middle lobe drains with the foot of the bed raised about 16 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist assesses a patient's voice sounds as part of a respiratory examination. Which condition is typically associated with increases voice sounds?
questions.explanation: Increased voice sounds (bronchophony) occur over consolidated lung.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Restrictive lung diseases limit to varying degrees the maximum volume of air that can be inhaled and exhaled. Examples of restrictive diseases include all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Emphysema is an obstructive disease, not restrictive.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist's emphasis when treating a child with _________ is aggressive bronchial drainage, chest vibration and percussion?
questions.explanation: Aggressive bronchial drainage, percussion and vibration are central in cystic fibrosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Exercise causes a significant increase in the body's cardiac output. During mild to moderate exercise what redistribution of the available cardiac output would you expect?

options.A: An increase in cerebral and coronary blood flow
options.B: A decrease in cerebral and active skeletal muscle blood flow
options.C: An increase in coronary and active skeletal muscle blood flow
options.D: A decrease in cerebral and coronary blood flow

questions.explanation: During exercise cardiac output is redistributed to the working skeletal muscle and the heart.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient in a pulmonary rehabilitation program is positioned in supine with a pillow under the knees. The therapist claps between the clavicle and nipple on each side. This technique is utilized for postural drainage of the:

options.A: Anterior segments of the upper lobes
options.B: Anterior basal segments of the lower lobes
options.C: Superior segments of the lower lobes
options.D: Posterior basal segment of the lower lobes

questions.explanation: Clapping between clavicle and nipple drains the anterior segments of the upper lobes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist reviews a laboratory report for a 41-year- old male diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Which of the following would be considered a normal hemoglobin value?
questions.explanation: A normal adult male haemoglobin is about 15 g/dL.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist positions a patient in prone with two pillows under the hips in preparation for bronchial drainage. If the therapist's goal is to perform bronchial drainage to the superior segments of the lower lobes, which area should the therapist's force be directed.

options.A: Between the clavicle and nipple on each side
options.B: Over the area between the clavicle and top of the scapula on each side of the spine
options.C: Over the lower ribs on each side
options.D: Over the middle of the back at the tip of the scapula on each side of the spine

questions.explanation: Superior segments of the lower lobes are percussed over the mid-back at the scapular tip.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Secretion removal techniques are often a necessary component of a pulmonary rehabilitation program. Which pulmonary disease is usually associated with a change in the composition of secretions?
questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis changes the composition of secretions (thick and sticky).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist performs a respiratory assessment on a patient with restrictive lung disease. If the therapist records the respiration rate as 22 breaths per minute, which term is most appropriate to classify the patient's respiration rate?
questions.explanation: A rate of 22 breaths per minute is tachypnoea.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to auscultate over the aortic valve. Which of the following areas is the most appropriate to isolate the desired valve?

options.A: Second left intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: Second right intercostals space at the right sternal border
options.C: Fourth left intercostals space along the lower left sternal border
options.D: Fifth left intercostals space at the midclavicular line

questions.explanation: The aortic valve is auscultated at the second right intercostal space.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes a pulmonary function test on a male patient admitted to the hospital three days age. Assuming normal valves, the patient's residual volume should be approximately_______ percent of the total lung capacity?
questions.explanation: Residual volume is about 25% of total lung capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist positions a patient for bronchial drainage to the anterior segments of the upper lobes. The most appropriate patient position is:

options.A: Supine with a pillow under the knees
options.B: Supine with the head of the bed elevated 16 inches
options.C: Supine with the foot of the bed elevated 16 inches
options.D: Supine with the foot of the bed elevated 16 inches E. Prone with the head of the bed elevated 12 inches

questions.explanation: Anterior segments of the upper lobes drain in supine with a pillow under the knees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to estimate the energy expenditure in calories for a cardiac patient performing a selected activity for 15 minutes. Assuming the therapist has a metabolic equivalent value for the activity, what other variables are necessary in order to obtain an estimate of the patient's energy expenditure?

options.C: Patients stroke volume and heart rate
options.D: Patient's residual volume and heart rate

questions.explanation: Estimating calories from METs requires the patient's weight and oxygen consumption.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist outlines a walking program for a patient rehabilitating from a prolonged illness. Which of the following recommendations would not be beneficial to the patient?

options.A: Wear comfortable, loose fitting clothing appropriate for the present temperature and weather
options.B: Walk at a rate designed to bring the heart to target levels
options.C: Walk continuously; frequent stops interfere with aerobic training
options.D: When walking up steep hills lean back ward slightly and lengthen your stride

questions.explanation: Leaning backward on steep hills is poor advice; lean forward and shorten the stride.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist designs a general fitness program for a senior citizen group. Which of the following guidelines is not accurate?

options.A: Allow participants the opportunity to reduce the intensity of exercise
options.B: Exercise intensity should be at a level which will provide a training effect
options.C: Exercise should be performed daily for at least 30 minutes
options.D: Exercise activities should include a warm-up and cool-down period

questions.explanation: Daily 30-minute exercise is not required; 3-5 days per week is adequate.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: On chest X-ray the silhouette sign presents as:

options.A: The two separate structures adjacent to each other are not identified because of lack of difference in bone densities
options.B: Paralysis of diaphragm over shadows the lung
options.C: Enlargement of cardiac field in the transverse direction
options.D: A sharp contrast between two adjacent

questions.explanation: The silhouette sign is loss of the border between adjacent structures of similar density.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: PEEP in chest care physiotherapy refers to:

options.C: Positive endurance exercise for pulmonary performance
options.D: Peak myography and electrocardiography of pulmonary performance

questions.explanation: PEEP stands for positive end-expiratory pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The ratio of chest compression to manual ventilation for a single rescuer in CPR is:
questions.explanation: Single-rescuer CPR in older guidelines used 15 compressions to 2 breaths.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist employed in a nursing home routinely treats patients in excess of 70 years of age. The therapist has noted several consistent postural changes in her patients. Which of the following does not accurately describe the postural changes associated with aging?
questions.explanation: Ageing increases hip flexion (not hip extension), with forward head, rounded shoulders and flexed knees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/Pg. 429-430

questions.question: A therapist provides exercise guidelines for a group of expectant mothers. Contraindications for exercise during pregnancy include all of the following except.
questions.explanation: Diastasis recti is a precaution for abdominal exercise, not an absolute contraindication.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist reviews the results of a complete blood count taken on a 65-year-old male recently admitted to the hospital. Which of the following blood test values may be considered a precaution for therapeutic exercise?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin of 8 g/dL is a precaution for therapeutic exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A female distance runner complains of recurrent friction blisters whenever she increases the intensity of her training regimen. Appropriate physical therapy care of friction blisters includes all of the following except:

options.A: Pad the blister with a pressure pad
options.B: Use of skin tougheners with astringents
options.C: Soak regularly in ice water after activity
options.D: Make a large incision along the periphery of the blister with a sterile instrument

questions.explanation: Friction blisters are not incised; padding and prevention are used.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Effective measures to prevent decubitus ulcers include all of the following except:

options.A: Frequent inspection of the skin for redness and signs of skin breakdown
options.B: Tsurning and position changes every 4 hours

questions.explanation: Repositioning is required at least every 2 hours, not 4.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The optimal position for a patient who begins to demonstrate signs of orthostatic hypotension is:
questions.explanation: Lying supine is the best position for symptomatic orthostatic hypotension.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which of the following procedures is most commonly used to determine activity tolerance after myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: A graded exercise test determines activity tolerance after myocardial infarction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: On chest X-ray the SILHOUTTE sign presents as:

options.A: The two separate structures adjacent to each other are not identified because of lack of difference in bone densities
options.B: Paralysis of diaphragm over shadows the lung
options.C: Enlargement of cardiac field in the transverse direction
options.D: A sharp contrast between two adjacent Physiotherapy Gynae

questions.explanation: The silhouette sign is loss of the border between two adjacent structures of similar density.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient sustains a deep laceration on the right anterior thigh after stumbling and falling in a modality cart. The therapist's most immediate response should be to:

options.A: Apply direct pressure over the wound

questions.explanation: The immediate response to a bleeding laceration is direct pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Agent in Rehabilitation/Cameron/2nd Ed./Pg. 32

questions.question: In the event of cardiac arrest, the right step to follow immediately is:

options.A: Apply external cardiac massage and mouth to mouth breathing
options.B: Inform the head of the department

questions.explanation: In cardiac arrest start chest compressions and ventilation immediately.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
